model: TFF v2 - HYPOTHETICAL truly flying fish
units_and_axes: glTF Y-up; head at +X, back at +Y, the fish's left side at -Z. The adult / resolved set has SL = 0.82 model units; earlier growth stages are built at their TRUE relative size SL(age)/SL(adult), so development plays as real growth. standard_length_m = 0.2030 m sets the metres per model unit.
MORPHOLOGICAL_NOT_GENETIC: MORPHOLOGICAL edit, not a genetic modification. This design is ONE parent (flying-fish) with its parameters moved by the named deltas; a delta is a change to a shape, not an allele, a pathway or a developmental programme, and nothing here says such an animal could be bred, is viable or is developmentally reachable. This is a shape, not an organism. Its growth stages are NOT data: they are the flying fish's growth with the deltas ramped in on an assumed schedule (stages.json 'tff'.assumption).
generative_model: parameters = SUM over parents ( weight_i * parent_i.parameter ) + delta

lean_recheck.why: a design inherits whatever constraints its parents satisfy; every delta needs re-checking

body_mass_kg.drives: wet mass; with flight_muscle_fraction sets the girdle muscle volume

body_depth_over_SL.drives: maximum body depth / SL (full depth, not half)

body_section_exponent.drives: superellipse exponent of the trunk cross-section (2 = ellipse)

head_fraction_SL.drives: fraction of SL over which the snout rounds off

peduncle_depth_frac.drives: caudal peduncle depth / maximum body depth

peduncle_width_frac.drives: caudal peduncle width / maximum body width

pectoral_len_over_SL.drives: longest pectoral fin ray, base to tip, / SL

pectoral_span_over_SL.drives: pectoral tip-to-tip span / SL (both fins, across the body)

delta.reason: TFF span 0.66442 m (= sqrt(9 * W / 12), physics/flier/design.py) over the real fish's measured 0.261 m (Park & Choi L3). Body SL unchanged, so the span RATIO carries the whole change.

pectoral_area_over_SL2.drives: area of BOTH pectoral fins together / SL^2 (Park & Choi 2010 A1 = planform area of the pectoral fin PAIR; their mean chord c = A1/S over the full span S confirms A1 covers both fins)

delta.reason: lifting area 0.04905 m2 at wing loading 12 N/m2 over the real reference area 0.012688 m2. The multiplier is applied to EVERY lifting surface (pectoral, pelvic, caudal) so the TOTAL lifting area hits the spec and the surfaces keep their measured proportions.

pectoral_ray_count.drives: lepidotrichia per pectoral fin (one named mesh each)

delta.reason: same area multiplier, taken on the linear dimension (sqrt), so the pelvic planform scales with the rest

flight_muscle_fraction.drives: pectoral/girdle muscle mass / body mass; sets the VOLUME of pectoral_muscle_L/R, so it visibly thickens the girdle musculature

delta.reason: physics/flier/tff/tff.json tff.muscle.fraction = 0.16, aerobic (red) flight muscle. Above the bat mean 0.0913 (PMC10966098); no fish value exists.

mesh_detail.drives: global mesh resolution multiplier (1.0 = the committed flying-fish detail)

derived_from_the_mesh.flight_muscle_note: the pectoral girdle musculature is sized by VOLUME from flight_muscle_fraction x body_mass, then clipped to what fits inside the skin. fit_fraction < 1 means the requested muscle mass does not fit in this body at this schematic geometry.
derived_from_the_mesh.measured_how: areas are membrane surface areas measured on the exported mesh; span is the tip-to-tip extent of the pectoral fins in the spanwise axis. The physical values use standard_length_m / 0.8200 model units.

definitions.pectoral_aspect_ratio: = span2_over_area_both (kept under this name for existing readers): tip-to-tip pectoral span^2 / area of BOTH pectoral fins together. This IS the Park & Choi 2010 convention, AR = S^2/A1 with A1 the planform area of the fin pair (L3: 0.261^2/0.006377 = 10.68). Before 2.0.0 this text wrongly said 'area of ONE fin'; the number was always the both-fins arithmetic.
definitions.span2_over_area_both: tip-to-tip pectoral span^2 / area of BOTH pectoral fins together = Park & Choi 2010 AR (S^2/A1)
definitions.aspect_ratio_one_fin: (span/2)^2 / (area of ONE pectoral fin) = span2_over_area_both / 2: one fin treated as a wing from the body midline to its tip. No fetched source uses it; it is here so 'one-fin AR' has one unambiguous meaning. NOTE span^2 / one-fin area (= 2 x Park & Choi) matches no source and is not stored.
definitions.span2_over_wing_area_fish1990: tip-to-tip pectoral span^2 / (both pectoral + both pelvic fin areas): Fish 1990's AR, whose 'wing area' is pectoral + pelvic fins plus the body rectangles between each fin pair (J Zool 221:391, Methods). The body rectangles are not modelled, so this is an UPPER BOUND on the Fish-1990 value. Fish's 3.0-16.9 range is in this convention, not Park & Choi's.
definitions.lifting_area_m2: pectoral (both) + pelvic (both) + caudal membrane area measured on the mesh. NOTE: physics/flier's reference area 0.012688 m2 is Park & Choi's A = A1 + A2 + A3, where A3 = 0.004474 m2 is the BODY planform, not the caudal fin; the mesh's caudal membrane stands in for A3 here (see CHANGELOG 2.0.0, open item)
definitions.flight_muscle_volume_m3: flight_muscle_fraction * body_mass / 1060 kg/m3 (teleost muscle density, assumed)

derived_from_the_mesh.aspect_ratio_note: pectoral_aspect_ratio == span2_over_area_both == Park & Choi 2010's AR = S^2/A1 (A1 = BOTH pectoral fins; the L3 fish is 10.68). aspect_ratio_one_fin = (S/2)^2 / one fin's area = half of it. span2_over_wing_area_fish1990 divides by pectoral + pelvic area, Fish 1990's 'wing area' without the body rectangles between the fins, so it is an upper bound on a Fish-1990 AR; Fish's 3.0-16.9 range is in that convention. Definitions and evidence: design-schema.json aspect_ratio_conventions.

parameter_vs_mesh_check.what: the parameters ask for a span and an area; these are what the exported MESH actually has
parameter_vs_mesh_check.verdict: fit applied; the mesh is solved to the span and area parameters

MISMATCHES_FOUND: DEFINITION MISMATCH in the spec itself: physics/flier/design.py keeps 'the fish's own aspect ratio' at 9.0-10.7 from Park & Choi, where AR = span^2 / A1 with A1 the area of BOTH pectoral fins (0.261^2 / 0.006377 = 10.68). It then applies 9.0 to the TOTAL LIFTING AREA A1+A2+A3 to get the span (span = sqrt(9 * W / 12)). Those are two different aspect ratios. On the real fish's own numbers span^2 / (A1+A2+A3) is 5.37, not 10.7. Read the TFF's AR 9.0 as span^2/total-lifting-area; in Park & Choi's convention (both pectoral fins) it is 17.9, 1.7x the measured L3 specimen's 10.68. CORRECTED in generator 2.0.0: an earlier version said this made its fins 'more slender than any measured flying fish', comparing 17.9 with Fish 1990's 3.0-16.9. That comparison mixed conventions: Fish 1990 divides span^2 by pectoral + pelvic area plus the body between them (Methods), which on the TFF gives at most 13.9 (pelvic included, body rectangles not modelled), INSIDE Fish's range; the L3 fish is <= 8.29 on Fish's convention, matching Fish's Cypselurus regression (~8.0 at 0.06 kg).

ROUNDING: the round multipliers x3.9 (area) and x2.5 (span) give wing loading 11.90 N/m2 and AR 8.60, not 12.0 and 9.0. This build uses the exact ratios 0.04905/0.012688 = 3.865857 and 0.664421/0.261 = 2.545674, which reproduce 12.0 and 9.0.

TWO READINGS OF THE SPEC, AND NO MESH SATISFIES BOTH. (A) built here: the area multiplier 3.865857 is applied to EVERY lifting surface, so total lifting area = 0.04905 m2 and wing loading = 12.0 N/m2 exactly, span^2/total = 9.0 exactly, and the pectoral-only AR comes out at 17.9. (B) the alternative: put ALL the extra area in the pectorals, giving pectoral area 0.04905 m2 and pectoral AR = 0.664421^2/0.04905 = 9.0, which matches Park & Choi's own pectoral-AR convention - but then the total lifting area is 0.05536 m2 (pelvic and caudal stay real-sized) and wing loading falls to 10.63 N/m2, not 12.0. The spec names 12 N/m2 as the design decision, so (A) is shipped. This is the mismatch, not a build error.

FLIGHT MUSCLE DOES NOT FIT: a flight-muscle fraction of 0.16 of 0.06 kg is 9.06e-6 m3 of muscle at 1060 kg/m3. Only 30% of that volume fits inside the flying fish's body at the pectoral girdle in this geometry; the rest was clipped. That is a geometric result of the spec, not a modelling choice, and it is the single most interesting thing the mesh says about the design.

adult_mass.what: the TFF spec mass (0.060 kg, the Park & Choi specimen, physics/flier/tff/tff.json) vs the borrowed flying-fish growth curve's adult (0.1316 kg); same two sources and roles as the flying fish, see flying-fish-dev-manifest.json adult_mass

base_resolved_set.source: Park & Choi 2010 J Exp Biol 213:3269, Table 1 model L3: ONE Cypselurus hiraii, body mass measured fresh before stuffing (physics/prior-art/raw/wb-park-choi-2010.txt); the paper gives mass to 0.01 kg, so 0.060 means 0.055-0.065
base_resolved_set.role: the base mesh's metres-per-unit, flight-muscle volume and derived wing loading. It is the mass physics/analysis.py uses for v_min = 9.85 m/s, because W, the fin areas and C_L,max all come from that one specimen and the paper reports its tunnel lift at 0 deg matching that weight (Fig. 4). Do not swap it for the growth-series mass in glide arithmetic: the areas and C_L,max belong to the 0.060 kg animal.

growth_series_adult.source: development/trajectory.mjs: von Bertalanffy SL(365 d), and W = 0.0116 FL^3.01 with FL = SL / 0.927 (Hirundichthys affinis, Barbados, FishBase; physics/length-weight.csv)
growth_series_adult.role: mass of a TYPICAL adult on the population curve, used only for the stage targets (flight-muscle volume per stage), so the series is smooth from hatchling to adult

adult_mass.is_it_units_or_definitions: No. Checked against the sources: both lengths are STANDARD length (Park & Choi Table 1 'Standard length, SL'; the trajectory converts the fork-length fit with SL/FL 0.927, and FL > SL, so the conversion cannot inflate mass by 2x); both masses are wet (fresh) mass in kg (Park & Choi weighed before stuffing, never frozen or fixed). Species differs (C. hiraii vs H. affinis) but that does not explain it either: every fitted exocoetid length-weight relation in physics/length-weight.csv gives 111-166 g at this size (Cheilopogon atrisignis n=570: 130 g; C. unicolor n=1640: 115 g; Cypselurus poecilopterus n=2769: 166 g; H. oxycephalus n=682: 111 g; H. affinis Barbados: 126 g at SL 0.203 m), and Fish 1990 (J Zool 221:391, Table I, Cypselurus n=113, ethanol-preserved, so if anything light) gives SL = 0.460 M^0.355, i.e. 0.100 kg at SL 0.203 m. The L3 specimen is genuinely light for its length: condition factor 100 W / SL(cm)^3 = 0.72, against about 1.5 for the population fits. Cause not stated in the paper (it does say the five fish were chosen for similar size, after a day on ice).
adult_mass.impact_if_the_population_mass_were_used_: wing loading on A1+A2+A3 = 0.012688 m2: 46.4 -> 101.7 N/m2; v_min = sqrt(2W/(rho S C_Lmax)) scales as sqrt(mass): 9.85 -> 14.6 m/s (Fish 1990's 0.100 kg: 12.7 m/s). The pre-registered envelope verdict B (inside if 20 >= v_min and 10 <= 3 v_min) stays 'inside' for any mass up to 0.247 kg, but the sentence 'quoted speeds 10-20 m/s are at or above the 9.9 m/s minimum' would no longer hold at the low end. Not changed here: physics/ is the physics thread's.

wing_loading_on_this_mesh_N_m2.how: mass * 9.81 / lifting_area_m2, the stage's area scaled by (SL ratio)^2 from the base mesh

basis.SL_and_mass: measured/secondary fits: von Bertalanffy (Oxenford 1994 via FishBase) x SL/FL 0.927, and W = 0.0116 FL^3.01 (physics/length-weight.csv). Below 14 d the SL curve is an ASSUMED linear ramp from an assumed 0.4 cm hatch length.

basis.pectoral_rays: ASSUMED ABSENT: below 1.68 cm SL the fin is modelled as a fold + endoskeletal disc (zebrafish proxy: Hale 2014, Grandel 1998, Lalonde 2018). Rays shrunk to 2%.

basis.body_depth: ASSUMED: held at the adult value 0.17 SL (itself an assumed, schematic number) at every stage. The repository holds no flying-fish body-depth measurement at any size (searched development/, physics/, genotype/, organisms/ on 2026-10-31). Early stages are therefore adult-shaped but small, which is wrong in detail and is the largest honest gap here.
parts_present: pectoral fin
pectoral fin fold + endoskeletal disc (larval fin)
yolk sac (absorbed within the first ~2 weeks)
pelvic fins enlarged ("wings"; about equal to pectorals in H. affinis larvae)
basis.THE_STATED_ASSUMPTION: growth curve borrowed from the flying fish; the TFF has no developmental data
basis.how_the_deltas_were_ramped: delta strength 0.0000 = (finRatio(age) - finRatio(hatch)) / (finRatio(adult) - finRatio(hatch)), i.e. the TFF is assumed to acquire its extra wing area, span and flight muscle on exactly the schedule on which a real flying fish acquires its measured pectoral-fin proportion. At hatching the TFF therefore equals a real flying-fish hatchling and the invention becomes visible as it grows. Nothing about this ramp is measured.
basis.why_this_construction: The alternative constructions considered were (a) show only the adult, which hides the question, and (b) apply the adult deltas at every age, which would put a 3.3 x SL wingspan on a 4 mm hatchling - a shape no developmental process produces and that we would be unable to defend. (c), used here, keeps the youngest stage identical to measured flying-fish larval morphology, so the ONLY invented quantity is the ramp of the deltas.
basis.what_is_NOT_claimed: that a TFF could develop, hatch, survive, or that the ramp resembles any real ontogeny. Development is not simulated anywhere in this project.
basis.flight_muscle_fraction: ramped 0.04 -> 0.16; the 0.16 endpoint is hypothetical (physics/flier/tff/tff.json) and the 0.04 start is an assumed placeholder - no measured pectoral-muscle mass fraction exists for any flying fish.

basis.fin_span_and_area: carried from the adult by the fin-length ratio (span linear, area ^1.834, Davenport 1992): an assumed transfer, not a measurement at this size.
basis.pectoral_rays: rays present (within the Daane 1.68-24 cm SL range)
basis.vertebrae: ASSUMED: no flying-fish ossification sequence was found. Centra are faded in with SL and reach the full 40 at 3 cm SL. The COUNT 40 is itself illustrative.
basis.body_depth: ASSUMED: held at the adult value 0.17 SL (itself an assumed, schematic number) at every stage. The repository holds no flying-fish body-depth measurement at any size (searched development/, physics/, genotype/, organisms/ on 2026-10-31). Early stages are therefore adult-shaped but small, which is wrong in detail and is the largest honest gap here.
basis.adult_mass: population length-weight fit (0.1316 kg); the base mesh is the Park & Choi L3 specimen (0.06 kg at SL 0.203 m). Both kept with roles: manifest adult_mass.
parts_present: pectoral fin
pelvic fins enlarged ("wings"; about equal to pectorals in H. affinis larvae)
gonad mature
basis.THE_STATED_ASSUMPTION: growth curve borrowed from the flying fish; the TFF has no developmental data
basis.how_the_deltas_were_ramped: delta strength 1.0000 = (finRatio(age) - finRatio(hatch)) / (finRatio(adult) - finRatio(hatch)), i.e. the TFF is assumed to acquire its extra wing area, span and flight muscle on exactly the schedule on which a real flying fish acquires its measured pectoral-fin proportion. At hatching the TFF therefore equals a real flying-fish hatchling and the invention becomes visible as it grows. Nothing about this ramp is measured.
basis.why_this_construction: The alternative constructions considered were (a) show only the adult, which hides the question, and (b) apply the adult deltas at every age, which would put a 3.3 x SL wingspan on a 4 mm hatchling - a shape no developmental process produces and that we would be unable to defend. (c), used here, keeps the youngest stage identical to measured flying-fish larval morphology, so the ONLY invented quantity is the ramp of the deltas.
basis.what_is_NOT_claimed: that a TFF could develop, hatch, survive, or that the ramp resembles any real ontogeny. Development is not simulated anywhere in this project.
basis.flight_muscle_fraction: ramped 0.04 -> 0.16; the 0.16 endpoint is hypothetical (physics/flier/tff/tff.json) and the 0.04 start is an assumed placeholder - no measured pectoral-muscle mass fraction exists for any flying fish.

design_record.name: TFF v2 - HYPOTHETICAL truly flying fish
design_record.body_plan_statement: The body plan is the flying fish's, with the spec's wing area, span and flight-muscle fraction applied. Nothing here is anatomy: no such animal has been described, dissected or measured. EVERY piece is hypothetical.

pectoral_span_over_SL.reason: TFF span 0.66442 m (= sqrt(9 * W / 12), physics/flier/design.py) over the real fish's measured 0.261 m (Park & Choi L3). Body SL unchanged, so the span RATIO carries the whole change.

pectoral_area_over_SL2.reason: lifting area 0.04905 m2 at wing loading 12 N/m2 over the real reference area 0.012688 m2. The multiplier is applied to EVERY lifting surface (pectoral, pelvic, caudal) so the TOTAL lifting area hits the spec and the surfaces keep their measured proportions.

pelvic_len_over_SL.reason: same area multiplier, taken on the linear dimension (sqrt), so the pelvic planform scales with the rest

flight_muscle_fraction.reason: physics/flier/tff/tff.json tff.muscle.fraction = 0.16, aerobic (red) flight muscle. Above the bat mean 0.0913 (PMC10966098); no fish value exists.
